name: David Nahmad
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Megadealer David Nahmad owns a stockpile of modern and impressionist art, stored in a duty-free warehouse in Geneva, Switzerland.
Nahmad's inventory includes more than 30 blue chip artists, from Monet and Matisse to Renoir and Rothko. He buys and sells mainly at auction.
Among the holdings: 300 Picassos, worth at least $1 billion. The whole collection is worth an estimated $7 billion. He splits the art assets with the heirs of his late brother, Ezra.
David also trades a currency and stock portfolio worth more than $400 million.
forbes_facts: David's son Hillel runs the Helly Nahmad Gallery in the Carlyle Hotel in Manhattan. His nephew runs a gallery by the same name in London.
David's younger son Joe runs the Nahmad Contemporary gallery on Manhattan's Madison Avenue. His nephew, also named Joe, runs the Nahmad Projects gallery in London.

name: Rodney Sacks
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Rodney Sacks is chairman of energy drink maker Monster Beverage Corporation. He retired as co-CEO in June 2025.
Sacks and Monster's co-CEO Hilton Schlosberg, are native South Africans. They bought the drink company Hansen Natural in 1992.
Hansen Natural launched the Monster energy drink brand in 2002, and the company changed its name to Monster Beverage in 2012.
In 2015, Coca-Cola bought a 16.7% stake in Monster Beverage for $2.15 billion in cash and opened its global distribution network to Monster.
Coca-Cola and Monster went into arbitration in 2018 after Coca-Cola decided to develop two energy drinks of its own. Coca-Cola ultimately won.
forbes_facts: Before buying what became Monster, Sacks was a senior partner at Werksmans, one of the largest law firms in South Africa.
Sacks studied law at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa; he later became a U.S. citizen and lives in southern California.

name: Lin Ming-hsiung
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Lin Ming-hsiung is the chairman of PX Mart, one of Taiwan's largest supermarket chains.
He took over PX Mart from the government in 1998 when it had 66 outlets. Today it boasts over 1,200 stores as well as minimarkets that serve Taiwan's remote villages.
In 2022, the company completed a $377 million deal to purchase a 96% stake in hypermarket chain RT-Mart's Taiwan business.
Lin also controls real estate developer Yuanlih Construction and Hwatai Bank.

name: Wilhelm Beier
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Wilhelm Beier is the chairman of the supervisory board of Dermapharm, a pharmaceutical company he founded in 1991.
Dermapharm, based in Gruenwald near Munich, manufacturers generic drugs for maladies ranging from insect bites to fungal diseases and osteoporosis.
Nearly half of its revenues come from the so-called "parallel trade'': arbitraging price differences for drugs between countries.
Dermapharm, which went public in 2018, is expanding into the business of medical marijuana. Beier and his family still own more than 70% of the company.
The company holds over 40% of one Germany's most popular home shopping television channels.
forbes_facts: Wilhelm's wife Elisabeth runs the company's international business, while son Michael runs online perfume shop Point Rouge.
Known as "Willi" in Munich, Beier has reportedly hosted parties with celebrity guests at his estate in Kitzbuehel, Austria, one of the world's top ski resorts.

name: William Young
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: William Young is CEO of plastic container maker Plastipak, which does some $3.7 billion in annual sales.
Young and his father founded Plastipak in 1967, shortly after he graduated from the University of Detroit Mercy with an engineering degree
After six years of running the business, the duo sold the majority to Beatrice Foods for an undisclosed amount.
In 1982, the family bought back Plastipak. Three decades later, they sold a minority stake to a division of Goldman Sachs. They bought out Goldman by 2020.
forbes_facts: Plastipak holds over 500 U.S. patents for package design and manufacturing processes.
Plastipak manufactures plastic packaging for companies such as Procter & Gamble, Pepsi and Kraft Foods.

name: Steven Witkoff
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025)
forbes_bio: Steven Witkoff is the founder and chairman of Witkoff Group, a real estate development firm he founded in New York in 1997.
Witkoff Group's developments include luxury condos, hotels, golf courses and apartment buildings in New York, Los Angeles and Florida.
Friends with Donald Trump since the early 1990s, Witkoff was appointed as Trump's special envoy to the Middle East in November 2024.
As Middle East envoy, Witkoff helped negotiate a peace deal in Gaza between Israel and Hamas in October 2025.
In 2025, he was also tasked with negotiations to end the war in Ukraine and reach an agreement with Iran over its nuclear program.
Witkoff was a real estate lawyer and then started buying apartments and offices with his former colleague Larry Gluck before going it alone in 1997.
forbes_facts: Witkoff and his family own an estimated 6.4% interest Trump's crypto project World Liberty Financial.
Witkoff and Trump first met when Witkoff was a real estate lawyer in the late 1980s and Trump was a client; Witkoff bought him a sandwich.

name: Suhail Bahwan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2025)
forbes_bio: Suhail Bahwan is the founder and chairman of Suhail Bahwan Group, one of the largest conglomerates in Oman.
It is a major producer of fertilizers, generating 1.3 million tons of urea annually. It was the sole distributor for Nissan cars in Oman from 2004 until 2023, when Nissan ended the partnership.
He first went into business with his brother Saud in 1965, selling fishing nets and building materials, before scoring the Toyota dealership in 1975.
In 2002, he split with his brother, who kept the Toyota dealership and passed it along after his death to his son Mohammed.
forbes_facts: Bahwan attended primary school in India, but dropped out after sixth grade. He sailed a dhow, and sold dried dates and fish.
His daughter Amal is vice chair of the group. Another daughter, Hind, is the founder of an IT firm called CyberTek.

name: Tony Chen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2023)
forbes_bio: Tony Chen cofounded Largan Precision, a lens supplier to Apple and other tech outfits, with fellow billionaire Scott Lin.
He stepped down as chairman in 2013 and sat on the board until 2022.
The company is a leading smartphone lens maker and a major supplier to Apple, claiming a quarter of the global market.

name: Pawel Marchewka
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Pawel Marchewka is the founder and CEO of Polish videogame company, Techland.
Founded in 1991, Techland is the publisher of zombie-themed titles including the Dead Island and Dying Light franchises.
Techland was sold to Chinese technology giant Tencent in 2024 for a reporrted 6.9 billion zloty ($1.7 billion).
The sale to Tencent came on the heels of news about internal struggles and layoffs at the gaming company.

name: Dilip Surana
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2016-2019)
forbes_bio: Dilip Surana is chairman of privately held pharma company Micro Labs, known for its popular paracetamol Dolo 650.
The Bangalore-headquartered generics company makes drugs for cardiac diseases, diabetes and pain management.
It also makes ophthalmic products for Bausch & Lomb's Asia-Pacific market.
The company gets nearly 60% of its annual revenue of from the domestic market.
The company was founded by their late father G.C. Surana, a former pharma distributor, in 1973 in Chennai.
forbes_facts: During the pandemic, sales of their paracetamol brand Dolo 650 soared.
India's tax authority alleged in July 2022 that Micro Labs gave freebies worth 10 billion rupees to doctors to push drug sales. The company denied any wrongdoing.
